nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / sandbox testing costs
Legacy Oracle data migration tooling and DBA consulting
Cloud infrastructure (staging + production) setup for CI/CD

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available yet for this project; estimate is built bottom-up from story points and role rates, not from prior delivery data.

Story points converted to hours at roughly 6-7 hours/point for backend-heavy items, adjusted for role mix and task complexity (e.g. legacy migration and payment integration weighted higher per point due to risk/integration overhead).

Backend Developer (1.5 FTE) carries the largest share of hours (auth, RBAC, payments, migration, APIs); at ~1100 hours this is roughly 4.5 months of combined capacity for the 1.5 FTE team, which is tight given the backlog size — flagged as a risk of under-staffing relative to scope.

Frontend Developer (1.0 FTE) hours (760) cover component library, dashboard, invoice UI, accessibility, responsive layout, and admin back-office screens; this role is also heavily loaded relative to 1.0 FTE capacity.
QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) hours (420) assume QA works across all urgent/high items plus a pass on medium items; low-priority items get lighter QA coverage.
DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) hours (170) cover CI/CD setup, staging environment, and observability/tracing; this is a thin allocation and assumes no major infra incidents.
Non-labour costs include third-party accessibility audit, Stripe sandbox/integration costs, legacy Oracle migration tooling/DBA consulting, cloud infra setup, and a small contingency buffer.
Scenario range (Optimistic/Most Likely/Pessimistic) reflects uncertainty in the legacy migration (PW-8) and payment integration (PW-7) effort, which are the two highest-risk items.
Low-priority items (PW-12, PW-18, PW-19, PW-23, PW-24) are included in the baseline estimate but are the first candidates for descoping if budget needs to be reduced.
Estimate assumes a single delivery team with no parallel workstreams beyond the stated FTE capacity, and no significant scope changes during delivery.
input.reasoning: Effort was sized bottom-up per backlog item using story points as a proxy for relative complexity, then mapped to role hours based on which roles are naturally involved in each task (e.g. PW-8 migration is backend+devops heavy, PW-2/PW-15/PW-20 are frontend heavy, all items carry a QA pass). Total hours were checked against each role's FTE capacity over an assumed ~5-6 month delivery window to sanity-check feasibility; Backend and Frontend are the most heavily utilized roles and are called out as tight. Labour lines were reconciled against the rate card (exact rates, cost = hours x rate) via check_estimate. Non-labour costs cover the concrete external spend items implied by the backlog (Stripe, Oracle migration tooling, accessibility audit, cloud infra) plus a small contingency. Three scenarios (P10/P50/P90) reflect uncertainty concentrated in the two highest-risk/highest-point items (legacy migration and payment integration), with the Most Likely scenario reconciled exactly to the sum of the line items.

reductions.description: Descope or defer low-priority items (PW-12 Support ticket submission, PW-18 Admin back-office, PW-19 Usage analytics, PW-23 Contract tests, PW-24 Decommission legacy portal) to a later phase.
reductions.effect: Removes all Low-priority backlog items from this delivery phase; reduces Backend/Frontend/QA hours proportionally.

reductions.description: Reduce Multi-currency support (PW-14) scope to USD+EUR only at launch, adding PLN later.
reductions.effect: Cuts backend and QA effort on FX handling and settlement logic by roughly a third.

reductions.description: Defer Usage analytics/reporting and Audit log to post-launch and rely on basic application logs initially.
reductions.effect: Removes dedicated backend/frontend build-out for PW-10 and PW-19 from the initial release.

reductions.description: Reduce third-party accessibility audit to an internal self-assessment against WCAG 2.2 AA instead of an external paid audit.
reductions.effect: Removes the external audit non-labour line item; relies on internal QA/Frontend testing instead.

reductions.description: Delay Observability tracing/dashboards (PW-22) beyond payment-path basics until after go-live.
reductions.effect: Reduces DevOps hours allocated to full tracing/dashboard build-out, keeping only minimal payment-path alerting.
